findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review. Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days.
findings.fix: Split the section into subsections labeled by role (e.g., 'What Employees Do' and 'What Managers Do'), or rewrite in consistent perspective for a single audience.
findings.violation: The section addresses both employees and managers without clarifying which reader each instruction targets. 'You' shifts meaning, and 'Countersign' appears without a stated subject.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Rewrite the paragraph to open with the coordination idea. Move the audit, federal guidance, and budget tangents to separate sections or omit them entirely.
findings.violation: The paragraph opens with a coordination statement, then abandons the topic entirely. Three unrelated details (audit, guidance, budget) follow with no signal that they relate to the opening sentence.

findings.evidence: How to Apply (lines 17-23) describes the request process. Later, Request Steps (lines 55-57) restates the beginning of the process. Terminology Notes (lines 49-53) appears before Request Steps.
findings.fix: Move Request Steps immediately after How to Apply, or consolidate them. Move Terminology Notes to an appendix or integrate its role-specific content into the relevant sections.
findings.violation: The document's section order does not follow the reader's actual task sequence. The request process is described twice in non-consecutive sections, disrupting the flow.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.
findings.fix: Rewrite the opening sentence to state the topic the rest of the paragraph covers.
findings.violation: The paragraph's opening sentence shares almost no vocabulary with the rest of the paragraph, so it does not preview the paragraph's actual topic.

findings.evidence: The stipend request...moves to final processing (line 21). An incomplete request pauses the timeline (line 29). The stipend pays up to 500 dollars per benefit year (line 39). Unused stipend amounts do not roll over to the next benefit year (line 42). The policy applies to one device per category per employee (line 47). Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility (line 57).
findings.fix: Replace abstract subjects with the real actors: 'The manager and finance team move the request...' instead of 'The request moves...'; 'You receive up to $500...' instead of 'The stipend pays...'; 'Your request restarts when you return...' instead of 'Completing the request begins...'
findings.violation: Six sentences name abstract nouns (request, stipend, amounts, policy, completing) as grammatical subjects instead of the real-world actors (people or organizations) performing the actions. Readers cannot tell who is responsible for each step.

findings.evidence: The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout. A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter.
findings.fix: Remove the audit, federal-guidance, and budget sentences. If they are relevant, move them to separate sections with their own headings and coherent topics.
findings.violation: The section titled Program Coordination introduces three unrelated themes (coordination, travel audits, remote-work guidance, office budgets) with no connecting logic. A reader cannot identify a single coherent topic the section is about.

findings.evidence: You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review. Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days. You track its status there until the payment clears.
findings.fix: Split into separate paragraphs by role. Keep each paragraph's subject consistent - do not jump between 'you,' 'Finance,' 'Payroll,' and imperative commands without clarification.
findings.violation: The paragraph's subjects shift rapidly and without signal (you → Finance → Payroll → you → imperative → you), breaking topic cohesion. Readers cannot follow what the paragraph's running topic actually is.

findings.evidence: A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests (line 33). Additionally, employees must retain receipts for one year after the purchase date (line 35).
findings.fix: Use one term consistently: either 'receipt' or 'proof of purchase' throughout. Add a defined-terms note if both are used intentionally.
findings.violation: The same documentation requirement is called both 'proof of purchase' and 'receipts' without signaling that these terms are synonymous.

findings.evidence: Also, the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing.
findings.fix: Move the interrupting clause elsewhere, or split it into its own sentence.
findings.violation: 3 comma-set-off clause(s) totalling 14 words intervene between the sentence's apparent subject and its verb.

findings.evidence: An incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives. The...
findings.fix: Open the paragraph with a transition word that states its relationship to the prior paragraph.
findings.violation: The paragraph opens with none of the fixed transition words, so the reader is not told how it relates to the paragraph before it.

findings.evidence: Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt.
findings.fix: Restate every item in the series with the same grammatical form.
findings.violation: The series' 2 items mix grammatical forms (gerund, other) at their head words instead of sharing one form.

findings.evidence: The stipend pays up to 500 dollars per benefit year.
findings.fix: Reorder to place the amount at the end: 'Each year, the company pays up to 500 dollars in equipment reimbursement' or 'Eligible employees receive up to 500 dollars per benefit year.'
findings.violation: The sentence's most important information (the dollar amount) appears in the middle, not at the end where reader emphasis lands. The final position is occupied by 'per benefit year,' a detail less important than the amount itself.
